review_notes:
I read the whole file and looked for substantial reasoning repeated across proofs. I found no duplication that meets the rubric. Candidates I considered and rejected:
- `abs_mul_div` and `locally_constant` each split on the sign of a real number. That is a short case split inside each proof, and moving it into a helper would only relocate the branches.
- `coefficient_chart` and `coordinateVolume_ne_zero` both apply a `TopForms` lemma to `inverseChartEquiv p z hz`, then run `erw [inverseChartEquiv_coe] at h`. They prove different statements and the common part is routine unfolding. A shared lemma would be a thin wrapper.
- `volumeSquare_contDiffOn` and `coefficient_smooth` both compose `(ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ _ ℝ v).contDiff` with `comp_contDiffOn`. This is a one-line use of existing API.
- Outside the file, `HodgeFiniteFrameResolution.lean` has a similar `erw [inverseChartEquiv_coe] at he; exact he` ending. It is a one-line rewrite and not a nontrivial repeated argument.
I could not run Lean, so I did not test any hypothetical refactor.
